mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in RSAFS (consumer savings) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates tighter monetary policy and reduced household liquidity, which depresses consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND RSAFS falls > 5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in HOUST and GDPC1 above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening housing demand and overall economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market growth, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises above 3% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it indicates inflationary pressure without a corresponding policy response, which erodes real equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
